title: Anchor shift capacity cribsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for anchor/night shift — keep short actionable items, command snippets, telemetry pointers, and fallbacks. Edited in-flight; treat as personal checklist and handoff notes.

Top-of-shift goals (30m):
- Check pool health dashboards (day/peak vs night) — look for sharp drops in active worker count or sudden full vram events.
- Confirm autoscaler is not oscillating: check last 2h scale events and CPU/GPU utilization windows.
- Validate routing fallback chain for hosted-inference (model-variants/v2->v1->cpu-approx).

Immediate checklist:
- [ ] Review `gpu-pool-prod-west-1` node count and pending pods (kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending).
- [ ] Drain any nodes stuck in `NotReady` for >10m (cordon + drain then open ticket).
- [ ] Restart flakily failing sidecar on pool edge gateways (kubectl rollout restart ds/edge-sidecar -n infra).
- [ ] Validate KV cache hit ratio for top-10 routes (console -> Optimize -> caching) — if <70% escalate.

Quick commands to copy: (keep minimal)
- kubectl -n inference get nodes -o wide | egrep "gpu|accelerator"
- kubectl -n inference describe pod <pod-name> | egrep "OOM|Evicted|GPU" -A3
- curl -sS "https://admin.redwood/api/v1/metrics?pool=gpu-pool-prod-west-1" | jq '.allocations[-10:]'

Telemetry & thresholds to watch:
- per-node GPU mem oversubscribe events >3/hour -> reduce max-concurrency on that node pool.
- prefix-cache hit rate drop >10% in 30m for top route -> temporary route pin to smaller model with warm cache.
- p95 latency increase >50ms and tokens/sec drop -> check batching and KV cache.

Routing fallback checks (manual):
- Confirm fallback policy exists for route `customer-api/stream-chat` (should fallback to replica v3-low-latency then v2).
- Verify that fallback logs show healthy fallbacks (search logs: "fallback_invoked route=customer-api/stream-chat")

Notes on capacity decisions tonight:
- We have a scheduled internal batch training job hitting the west pool at 02:00 UTC — temporary +8 GPUs reserved from burst-capacity until 04:00. If contention observed, move training to `training-spot-aux` or throttle to 60% concurrency.
- If sustained queue length > 40 for >15m, open quickpager and promote dedicated spare pool `dedicated-surge-1` (contact ops-runbook rotation).

Known flaky things (investigation TODOs):
- Node label mismatches: some nodes returned with label `zone:westa` instead of `zone:west-1` causing autoscaler rules to misapply. Root cause unknown. File ticket.
- Edge-sidecar OOMs correlated with binary bump on 2026-03-09 release. Need canary rollback plan if recurrence.

Handoff snippets for morning team:
- If I don't respond by 06:30 UTC, please:
  - escalate to Maya (pager) for sustained p95 > 800ms across routes.
  - capture a heapdump from sidecar on node <node-id> and attach to JIRA-OPS-2345.

Loose thoughts / brainstorm (not actioned yet):
- Could try a dynamic per-route concurrency cap computed from rolling token cost to lower tail latency without sacrificing throughput. Short experiment: add a dynamic limiter in front of top-5 routes for 12h and compare p99.
- Scripting idea: small lambda that monitors cache-hit tail and auto-pin route to warm caching if hit <60% for 15m. Quick PoC in `infra/scripts/cache-pin-probe`.

Links & references: (copy-paste for handoff)
- Pool dashboard: https://internal.redwood/infra/dashboards/gpu-pools
- Autoscaler logs (query): https://logs.redwood/search?q=autoscaler%20gpu-pool-prod-west-1
- Runbook (edit if you fix the label issue): confluence:gpu-pools-runbook

End-of-shift quick capture (fill before signout):
- Observed anomalies: 
  - node gpu-137 dropped last week; replaced, but still intermittent NVML timeout.
  - KV cache hit for customer-api/stream-chat = 54% at 05:10 UTC (investigate warmup).
- Actions I did: 
  - cordoned node gpu-141 and drained; reopened ticket with bench logs.
  - temporary route pin for customer-api/stream-chat to v3-low-latency for 45m.
- Outstanding followups: 
  - file ticket for node label normalization (assign to infra-labels team).
  - schedule short postmortem if NVML timeouts continue.

Random notes to self: 
- Remember to run the night billing check script (scripts/nightly/check-billing.sh) tomorrow morning.
- Don't forget to update pager rotation sheet if you swap with Maya.

Questions / open: 
- Who owns `training-spot-aux`? Need contact to coordinate moving training.
- Confirm if burst-capacity billing alert is set for >$1200/day when using dedicated-surge-1.

End.
